Title: Feeling Like Home
Content: The plane landed on the tarmac at the airport after an uneventful flight from San Juan. As they taxied to the gate, Mateo looked out the window at the strange landscape. He soaked it in, both eager and nervous to see his new home.

Uncle Damien met them at the baggage claim area and drove them to what was now home. The street in Queens where Uncle Damien parked was adjacent to the elevated train tracks. Mateo thought they only had subways in New York City, but as was obvious by looking at this overhead train system, he was wrong. As they got out of the car, the train rumbled and shook the earth as it careened past the station. Mateo thought to himself, “How are we ever going to sleep at night to this? It's certainly nothing like the soothing sound of the ocean.”

Luckily for them, Uncle Damien had offered them a place to stay. His apartment had `text(two)` small bedrooms and a rather large living room where Uncle Damien had set up a big curtain to separate it into `text(two)` sections.

That night after they were settled, Uncle Damien showed them around the neighborhood. Tall brick buildings lined both sides of the street. Underneath the elevated train were shops, restaurants, and street vendors selling their wares. Mateo did have to admit that some of this did feel familiar-the smell of the food, the goods sold by the vendors, the music trailing out the apartment windows, all felt like home.

You can find Little Colombia, Little India, Little Santiago, Little Italy, Chinatown, and all kinds of other micro-neighborhoods in New York City. It is a fascinating place. Questions flew through his mind: How would he ever fit in here? Would the people here be nice to him? Would he be able to make any friends? It was so different. There was no ocean, no palm trees, no sandy beaches.

The next morning seemed to come in a flash, and Mateo hardly even felt like he slept at all. The train, the noise, the anxiety of the move-it had all taken its toll on any kind of restful sleep that Mateo could hope for. “A little,” Mateo replied, not wanting to worry his mama. “I think it'll be okay,” he said boldly, trying to convince himself more than anything else. He grabbed a plate and dished up a serving of tortilla Española and fried plantains.
